content.title: Dan Levy Reveals His Dad Eugene’s Reaction to His First New TV Series After ‘Schitt’s Creek’ (Exclusive)
content.text: Eugene Levy and Dan Levy. Credit : John Salangsang/Shutterstock NEED TO KNOW Dan Levy revealed his dad Eugene Levy’s reaction to his new Netflix dark comedy series, Big MistakesThe show follows siblings pulled into organized crime, drawing inspiration from Dan's real-life dynamic with sister Sarah Levy“Anyone who has a sibling, I think, will recognize themselves in the show,” he told PEOPLE at the show’s premiere on April 6 Dan Levy’s dad, Eugene Levy, is already a big fan of his new Netflix show, Big Mistakes. Speaking with PEOPLE in an exclusive interview at the show’s red carpet premiere in New York City on April 6, the 42-year-old actor, writer and director said that his dad, Eugene, 79, flew in to be there for the big night. “He came all the way from Canada to support,” Dan said, adding that both his parents had already seen the show and are fans of the dark comedy. Dan Levy (middle) with his parents, Deborah Divine and Eugene Levy, at the 'Big Mistakes' premiere on April 6, 2026. Jason Mendez/Getty “They're already quoting lines from it, and they're very excited to watch it again. So, that's all I could ask for,” he continued. The show, which premiered on April 9 on Netflix, centers on siblings Nicky (Dan) and Morgan (Taylor Ortega), who get blackmailed into the world of organized crime. Dan told PEOPLE that the show’s chaotic comedy is in many ways inspired by his real-life early relationship with his sister, Sarah Levy. “We're in a far better place now that we're older and wiser,” he explained. “But … anyone who has a sibling, I think, will recognize themselves in the show. And it was really about authenticating the experience of that sibling dynamic and just exacerbating all of the bickering in the light of, like, intense criminal activity.” Siblings Sarah Levy and Dan Levy in 2023. Axelle/Bauer-Griffin/FilmMagic Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer​​, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories. “So my hope is that anyone that comes from a yelling family, anyone that has a sibling, and anyone that's curious about what it is to have a sibling or come from a yelling family will find a place in this show. I just love it so much,” Dan added. The Schitt’s Creek co-creator also shared that he feels his latest project captures something special both on-screen and behind the scenes. All I did was set the table for these people, and they ate. So, this is just the cherry on top of a really, really special experience, and I hope we get to tell this story for seasons and seasons and seasons,” he added.
